title: Compact span-tile drillsheet with correlation ribbon
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Problem: Engineers need a fast, scannable view for investigating noisy endpoints where full flame charts are too heavy. Current request drill flow forces vertical scrolling and context switching between a long timeline and a separate correlation panel. Goal: prototype a compact "drillsheet" composed of horizontally stacked compact 'span-tiles' that encode key span metadata at a glance plus a persistent 'correlation ribbon' showing causal lineage for the selected request. The drillsheet should let users quickly triage a noisy request stream, filter by correlation ID or tag, preview logs, and jump to full trace views when needed. Design constraints: maintain keyboard navigability and screen-reader friendliness, fit within standard console width (>= 1024px), work with up to 500 visible spans (virtualized), and render without blocking main thread. Success metrics: reduce mean time-to-identify root cause by 30% in internal dogfooding; <150ms hover reveal; prototype test SUS score >= 75.
decisions: Adopt 'span-tiles' as 48px-high compact rows that expand on hover to 120px for quick details
Correlation ribbon pinned to left; shows up to 5 hops with directional arrows and service badges
Persistent quickfilter bar (service, status, tag, correlation-id) remains sticky and supports keyboard focus
Prefetch minimal log snippet and first 3 span events for each tile; full events fetched on expand or open-flame
Use ARIA roles and announce expanded tile contents to screen readers; focus trap on open full-trace modal

acceptance_criteria: Span-tiles render in list view with correct service, duration, start timestamp, status, and first log line
Correlation ribbon shows correct parent/child lineage for selected request and allows jump-to-trace
Keyboard navigation: up/down to move, Enter to expand, E to open expanded details, Esc to close
Prototype performance: initial tile render < 250ms for 100 items on a standard dev machine; hover expand < 150ms
Accessible: expanded content is announced by screen reader and focus order preserved
